project_context: Transparent evidence-card RAG for AI-assisted CSRD / ESRS-style disclosure generation

design_notes.purpose: Define controlled ESRS G1 Business Conduct information needs using the same task-spec, deterministic query-bundle and shared-generation pipeline as E1. Requirement numbering follows the original 2023 ESRS Annex I.
not_frozen_here: task selection pending evidence and retrieval checks
source validation and document eligibility for the expanded corpus

tasks.task_name: Business conduct policies and corporate culture
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about business-conduct policies, corporate culture, code of conduct, reporting channels, whistleblower protection, policy scope, and responsible functions.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests governance commitments and policy boundaries. Detailed anti-corruption procedures and training performance are reserved for G1-3.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 7-11. Business conduct policies and corporate culture.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: Historical codes of conduct and governance or compliance report sections are candidate sources. A hotline does not by itself establish anonymity, non-retaliation or independent investigation.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about business-conduct policies, corporate culture, code of conduct, reporting channels, whistleblower protection, policy scope, and responsible functions.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about business conduct policies and corporate culture using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Business-conduct policies and code of conduct
Development, promotion and assessment of corporate culture
Mechanisms for reporting concerns
Whistleblower protection and measures against retaliation
Policy training, responsibilities and coverage
Animal-welfare policy where applicable and evidenced
claim_risk_notes: Do not infer an effective ethical culture from the existence of a code.
Distinguish confidential reporting, anonymity and protection against retaliation.
Do not infer independent investigation from an externally operated hotline.
Do not claim universal employee or supplier coverage without evidence.
Do not substitute board diversity or remuneration under ESRS 2 GOV for G1 business conduct.

tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about supplier relationship management, procurement risks, social and environmental selection criteria, supplier assessment and development, and policies to prevent late payment, especially to SMEs.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Adds substantive supply-chain management coverage and prevents the four-task governance set from consisting entirely of internal compliance disclosures.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 12-15; application requirements AR 2-3. Management of relationships with suppliers.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: BASF and Evonik 2023 reports contain supplier selection, assessment, training and development evidence. The core is management practice; full payment-performance measurement belongs to G1-6.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about supplier relationship management, procurement risks, social and environmental selection criteria, supplier assessment and development, and policies to prevent late payment, especially to SMEs.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about management of relationships with suppliers using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Management of supplier relationships and procurement risks
Social and environmental supplier-selection criteria
Supplier screening, assessments and audits
Supplier engagement, development and corrective actions
Policies to prevent late payments, especially to SMEs
Supplier-assessment populations and denominators
claim_risk_notes: An audit or assessment does not establish that every supplier complies.
Preserve direct versus indirect supplier and spend-versus-supplier-count denominators.
Do not attribute all industry-initiative audits to the company.
Supplier-worker impacts belong to S2 unless used specifically as evidence of procurement management.
A payment policy or a threshold such as paid within 60 days is not an observed average payment time.

tasks.task_name: Prevention and detection of corruption and bribery
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery; investigator independence, reporting to governing bodies, policy communication and anti-corruption training.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests whether operational control and training claims are supported, while keeping allegations and incident outcomes in G1-4.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 16-21; application requirements AR 4-8. Prevention and detection of corruption and bribery.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The local catalogue contains 21 training-related indicator definitions and nonempty extracted cells in all 25 development company-years. General compliance training must be distinguished from anti-corruption training.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery; investigator independence, reporting to governing bodies, policy communication and anti-corruption training.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about prevention and detection of corruption and bribery using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery
Independence of investigators from implicated management
Reporting investigation outcomes to governing bodies
Communication of anti-corruption and anti-bribery policies
Nature, scope and depth of relevant training
Coverage of functions at risk and training of governing bodies
claim_risk_notes: Do not label all compliance training as anti-corruption training.
Do not confuse participants, unique people, completions, hours and coverage percentages.
Retain the correct denominator for functions at risk.
Do not infer control effectiveness or absence of corruption from training coverage.
Do not infer independence from an investigator's job title or external hotline operation.

tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about reporting-period corruption and bribery convictions, fines and actions addressing breaches; confirmed incidents, disciplinary measures, business-partner consequences and legal-case outcomes when disclosed.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Provides an incident-and-outcome task with substantively distinct allegation, confirmation and legal-status boundaries. Retention is conditional on a source audit because historical coverage is uneven.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 22-26. Incidents of corruption or bribery.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The local catalogue has five indicator definitions and nonempty extracted cells in only 10 of 25 development company-years. Evonik 2023 demonstrates that extracted values can mislabel alleged cases and general compliance outcomes as confirmed corruption.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about reporting-period corruption and bribery convictions, fines and actions addressing breaches; confirmed incidents, disciplinary measures, business-partner consequences and legal-case outcomes when disclosed.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about incidents of corruption or bribery using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Number of convictions and amounts of fines under anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws
Actions taken to address breaches in procedures and standards
Confirmed incidents and their nature where disclosed
Disciplinary measures, dismissals and business-partner consequences linked to corruption where disclosed
Public legal cases and reporting-period outcomes where disclosed
Incident status, reporting year, currency and company involvement
claim_risk_notes: Allegations, investigations, confirmed incidents and convictions are different statuses.
Do not treat all compliance dismissals or terminated contracts as corruption outcomes.
No convictions or no material cases does not establish no incidents.
Retain currency, reporting period, recognition basis and company involvement.
Do not treat missing evidence as zero, or a policy statement as an incident outcome.
A heading mentioning confirmed incidents cannot override qualifying text describing allegations.
